translation: What's this Dubai, what's this Muscat, my son, O Mallesha; why are you never to be seen, however long we wait, my child, my Mallesha? (What's this Dubai, what's this Muscat, my son, O Mallesha; why are you never to be seen, however long we wait, my child, my Mallesha?) What's this Dubai, what's this Muscat, my son, O Mallesha.

More than four years have passed since you left home; you didn't send a letter, you didn't even phone (you didn't even phone). How you are keeping, what you ate over there, how much hardship you face: we got to know none of it (we got to know none of it). Pining for you, your mother has lost her mind, son; every day she cries out for you, my child, O Mallesha.
(What's this Dubai, what's this Muscat, my son, O Mallesha; why are you never to be seen, however long we wait, my child, my Mallesha?)

You got your sister married and left, and you didn't send a single cowrie; the son-in-law demanded dowry and threw your sister out, child (threw your sister out, child). For the costs of farming the field we borrowed from the moneylender; the crop failed and troubles came, and the interest kept on growing (the interest kept on growing). Interest on interest has become compound interest, my son, O Mallesha; even if we sell the cattle, the house and the field, my child, the debt won't be cleared.
(What's this Dubai, what's this Muscat, my son, O Mallesha; why are you never to be seen, however long we wait, my child, my Mallesha?)

The debt you took on when you left was a lakh in principal, son; today it has doubled and sits on a mountaintop, child (sits on a mountaintop, child). Before you went abroad we held out our hand to no one; we lived like kings, son, and now our life has gathered cobwebs (now our life has gathered cobwebs). Wherever I look there is only mortal danger; what can I do, O Mallesha? I have come to fear life itself, my child, my Mallesha.

(What's this Dubai, what's this Muscat, my son, O Mallesha; why are you never to be seen, however long we wait, my child, my Mallesha?) Why are you never to be seen, however long we wait, my child, my Mallesha? Why are you never to be seen, however long we wait, my child, my Mallesha?
summaryEn:
Yemi Dubai Yemi ("What's This Dubai?") is a migration song addressed to Mallesha, a son who went to the Gulf, to Dubai or Muscat, more than four years ago and has not been heard from since. The speaker appears to be his father, since he refers to "your mother" in the third person, and each line is full of grief and exasperation. The chorus, "What's this Dubai, what's this Muscat", sounds almost like a curse on the faraway places that swallowed the son.

The verses give a detailed and painful account of what has happened at home. Mallesha has sent no letter, no phone call and no money. His mother has gone half-mad with worry and calls out for him every day. His sister, married off before he left, has been thrown out by her husband over unpaid dowry. The family borrowed from a moneylender to farm, the crop failed, and "interest on interest" has swelled the debt, including the lakh of rupees raised for his own journey, until selling cattle, house and land would not clear it. A family that once "lived like kings" now fears for its survival. The echoed phrases in brackets suggest a chorus answering the lead singer, and the song reflects the hard realities faced by many Telangana families whose men migrated to the Gulf.

ఏమి దుబాయ్ ఏమి అనేది వలస నేపథ్యంలోని పాట. నాలుగేళ్ళ క్రితం దుబాయ్, మస్కట్ వంటి గల్ఫ్ దేశాలకు వెళ్ళి అప్పటినుంచి ఏ కబురూ పంపని కొడుకు మల్లేశను ఉద్దేశించి ఇది పాడబడింది. "నీ తల్లి" అని మూడో వ్యక్తిగా ప్రస్తావించడం చూస్తే పాడేది బహుశా తండ్రే అనిపిస్తుంది; ప్రతి మాటలోనూ దుఃఖం, నిస్సహాయమైన కోపం కలిసి వినిపిస్తాయి. "ఏమి దుబాయ్ ఏమి మస్కట్" అనే పల్లవి కొడుకును మింగేసిన దూరదేశాలను తిట్టుకుంటున్నట్టే ధ్వనిస్తుంది.

ఇంటి దగ్గర జరిగిన కష్టాలను చరణాలు వివరంగా, గుండె పిండేలా చెబుతాయి. మల్లేశ నుంచి ఉత్తరం లేదు, ఫోను లేదు, చిల్లిగవ్వ కూడా రాలేదు. బెంగతో తల్లి పిచ్చిదై రోజూ అతన్నే కలవరిస్తోంది. అతను వెళ్ళేముందు పెళ్ళి చేసిన చెల్లెలిని కట్నం కోసం అల్లుడు ఇంట్లోంచి వెళ్ళగొట్టాడు. లాగోడి కోసం సేటు దగ్గర అప్పు తెస్తే పంట పండలేదు; వడ్డీకి వడ్డీ చక్రవడ్డీ అయి, అతని ప్రయాణం కోసం చేసిన లక్ష రూపాయల అప్పూ రెండింతలైంది — గొడ్డు గోదా, ఇల్లు, పొలం అమ్మినా బాకీ తీరని పరిస్థితి. ఒకప్పుడు ఎవరి ముందూ చేయి చాపకుండా రాజుల్లా బతికిన కుటుంబం ఇప్పుడు బతుకు మీదే భయపడుతోంది. బ్రాకెట్లలో మళ్ళీ వచ్చే మాటలు ప్రధాన గాయకుడికి కోరస్ బదులిస్తున్నట్టు సూచిస్తాయి. గల్ఫ్‌కు వలస వెళ్ళిన మగవాళ్ళ కుటుంబాలు తెలంగాణలో ఎదుర్కొన్న కఠిన వాస్తవాలను ఈ పాట ప్రతిబింబిస్తుంది.
